about: The rules the director follows. Change a value here, run tools/sketch_waves.py, and compare the waves it produces. Laws marked "in game" match the current Peacock Reef code; the rest are designed and used by the sketch tool until they are built in.
law_zero: Movement never changes catch chances or pays. Routes only decide where and when fish swim.

big_fish.what: Length of one big-fish wave. Runs on its own clock and pauses while a boss is on screen.
big_fish.try_next: Try 45-55 if the screen feels empty of big fish.

big_fish.what: One Shark every wave.
The Shark never enters from the same edge or travels the same direction two waves in a row.
How often each attitude is picked outside meetings.
big_fish.try_next: Raise Aggressive for a faster, harsher night.

big_fish.what: A Shark route is not reused until 4 other routes have run.
A Manta comes every other wave.
Chance a Manta visit becomes a Shark + Manta meeting. With the one-visit gap below this works out to about 1 visit in 3.
big_fish.try_next: Lower to .33 for rarer meetings (about 1 in 4).

big_fish.what: At least one plain Manta visit between meetings.
No meeting in the first 2 waves.
The only Shark routes allowed while a Manta glides.
How far (scaled pixels) the Shark lane must stay from the Manta remaining path; if nothing fits, the Shark waits.
Chance a meeting Shark brings a Shadow (never on a Grand arc).
Chance a non-meeting wave brings a second, smaller Shark (Shadow or Pincer).
Chance a wave has a Hammerhead.
big_fish.try_next: Lower to 1/2 if big fish take too much of the bullets.

big_fish.what: Chance a Hammerhead visit is a pair patrol on both seat rows.
Chance a wave gets a second Marlin.
Never more than 3 big fish at once.
Minimum gaps between big fish lanes.
A Marlin may cross a Shark lane only this long after the Shark passed.
A Hammerhead or Marlin that cannot find clear water for this long is dropped.
Small followers that travel with the Manta; they pull in to half their spread when a Shark is within 520 px.
Hits within the window that provoke Snap back or Frenzy.
How long big-fish time near each seat is remembered when routes are chosen.

medium_fish.what: No more than 2 fast fish (Tuna, Barracuda, Swordfish, Marlin) crossing the screen at once. A Crisscross counts as 2.
While a Shark crosses, at most this share of crossing mediums may go its direction; the rest go against it, vertical or stay local.
Score the sketch tool gives a crossing route that goes against or with the Shark.
Water a big fish will use in the next few seconds is off limits to mediums.
Minimum gap from that water, in screen fractions.
While a Shark splits the screen top to bottom, no medium crosses the center.
A medium never runs the same route twice in a row.
Hits that make an Octopus squirt ink and jet off (show only).
Pause between one visit of a species and its next.
Target fish on screen before scene mix and density settings.
How long medium time near each seat is remembered.
